# nonValidDomain

<link-summary>Checks whether a value is **not** a domain name.</link-summary>

<web-summary>nonValidDomain() — Checks whether a value is **not** a domain name. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>net/path</code> · Since: 1.11.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function nonValidDomain(domain: string): boolean;
```

`nonValidDomain(value)` is the same test as `!isValidDomain(value)`, written so that a guard clause reads as a sentence rather than as a negation.

Labels separated by single dots, with no leading or trailing dot or hyphen and no empty label. It is a syntax check: whether the domain resolves is another question.

`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type     | Description         |
| :-------- | :------- | :------------------ |
| `domain`  | `string` | The value to check. |

## Returns

`boolean` — `true` when the value is not a domain name; otherwise `false`.

## Examples

### What passes and what does not

```javascript
nonValidDomain("-example.com"); // => true
nonValidDomain("example..com"); // => true
nonValidDomain("example.com."); // => true
nonValidDomain(""); // => true
nonValidDomain("example.com"); // => false
nonValidDomain("sub.example.co.uk"); // => false
```
